prompt_package.goal_summary: Make a readable YouTube thumbnail with one clear face, one object and at most three words.

user_profile.who: Creator who uploads weekly and has no editor

blocks.task: Design a YouTube thumbnail for a video called {{video_topic}}. It must be readable on a phone at 160 pixels wide.
blocks.subject: {{person}} on the {{side}} of the frame, chest up, {{expression}}, eyes to camera. Beside them: {{hero_object}}.
blocks.scene: A simple {{background_style}} background, slightly darker than the subject so the silhouette pops. Strong empty space in the {{text_side}} third for the headline.
blocks.camera: 85mm portrait look, shallow but readable depth, subject sharp from hairline to shoulder.
blocks.light: Bright key light from the front left, soft fill, clear catchlights in the eyes, subtle rim light to separate hair from background.

text_in_image.placement: {{text_side}} third, upper area, aligned to the outside edge
text_in_image.style: very bold condensed sans, heavy weight, {{text_color}}
text_in_image.size: about one third of the frame height, two lines maximum

locks: The person's face, hair and skin tone match the attached photo exactly.
The headline is spelled exactly as written, all capitals, no extra words.
At most one graphic element besides the person and the object.
avoid: tiny text or more than three words
faces that look airbrushed or plastic
letters cut off by the frame edge

input_schema.description: Fill these before you run. Keep the headline to three words or fewer.

fields.name: video_topic
fields.example: How I fixed my sleep in 7 days

fields.name: person
fields.example: a man in his 30s wearing a dark green sweater

fields.name: expression
fields.example: surprised, eyebrows raised, slight open mouth

fields.name: hero_object
fields.default: a single simple prop that matches the topic

output_schema.description: What you get, plus a phone-size test.

fields.name: phone_test
fields.example: Shrink to 160px wide. Headline still readable? Keep. Not readable? Cut one word.

examples.title: Sleep video, cream text on navy

example_input.video_topic: How I fixed my sleep in 7 days
example_input.headline: SLEEP FIXED

examples.title: Budget cooking, yellow text on charcoal

example_input.headline: FIVE FOR $10
example_input.background_style: charcoal kitchen wall, softly out of focus

non_obvious_insights: State the phone test inside the prompt. 'Readable at 160 pixels wide' changes the model's size and spacing decisions.
Empty space must be requested as a named third of the frame. 'Leave room for text' usually produces a centered subject.
Three words maximum is a hard rule, not a style choice. Every extra word shrinks the rest.
Ask for catchlights in the eyes. They are the single strongest signal of a real, alive face.
Keep the face photo on a plain background. Busy backgrounds get blended into the new scene.
Naming an exact headline in quotes prevents the model from inventing filler words like 'AMAZING'.
Generate three expressions with the same everything else, then pick on a phone, not a monitor.
monetization_ideas: Sell a thumbnail subscription: 8 thumbnails a month, 48-hour turnaround, fixed price.
Productize a 'channel relaunch' pack: banner, 8 thumbnails, one consistent look.
Offer an A/B pair per video (two headlines), priced per pair. Creators pay for testable options.
Teach the method as a 40-minute workshop using this JSON as the handout.
prompt_package.reusability_notes: Same package works for podcasts (swap hero object for a microphone), course covers (change aspect_ratio to 1:1), and blog headers (21:9). Keep headline, expression and background as variables and you can mass-produce a season of covers. Swap 'YouTube thumbnail' in task for 'podcast cover' and the rest still holds.
